title: Water Kills Your Wi-Fi?! 📶
description: Wi-Fi is just radio waves carrying zeros and ones! Learn why walls and even a fish tank weaken your signal, and the difference between 2.4 and 5 GHz.

scenes.say: The internet reaches your phone through thin air, with no cable at all. So how does Wi-Fi work?
Your router takes data from the internet, turns it into radio waves, and your phone catches them and turns them back into data.

scenes.caption: Zeros and ones
scenes.say: Every photo and video you see is really zeros and ones, carried by tiny changes in the shape of the wave.
Most routers have two bands: two point four reaches farther but is slower, and five gigahertz is faster but has a shorter range.

scenes.text: Water and metal absorb Wi-Fi waves
scenes.say: Did you know water absorbs Wi-Fi waves? A fish tank, thick walls or metal can weaken your signal. So put your router high up and in the open.

scenes.text: Next: The internet under the sea!
scenes.say: Follow How It Works. Next time: the giant cables on the ocean floor that connect the whole world.
